text:
maria: Heads-up — ran a 24h run of the continuous-batcher with a soft-memory-watermark gate enabled on a single cluster (r4-gpu-pool). Wanted to share quick findings and get alignment before we bake this into canary.

sam: nice, what's the soft vs hard thresholds you used?

maria: soft=0.62 of KV pool, hard=0.78. soft=slow admission (reduce target tokens), hard=reject new batches if above. Also allowed 5% burst margin.

jay: curious about workload mix — did you replay prod traces or synthetic?

maria: replayed 3 days of prod traces (mixed chat + long-context embeddings). Replayed at ~1.4x QPS to stress.

perf-bot: Profiling summary (exec profile):
```
- baseline (no-gate): p95=85ms, avg GPU mem usage=72%, KV-frag=18%
- soft-gate: p95=92ms (+8%), avg GPU mem usage=66%, KV-frag=29%
- hard-gate: p95=120ms (+41%), request rejection rate ~2.2%, KV-frag=45%
flame: https://perf.internal/flame/1980012456
```

kei: fragmentation jump at soft gate looks concerning — 29% KV-frag implies many small evictions?

maria: yeah we saw KV slab churn — when we throttle token budgets the runtime keeps many short-lived KV entries from overlapping, which increases fragmentation.

sam: did kernel selection change during throttling? i.e., did we lose optimized kernel paths (cutlass) because sequence lengths shifted?

maria: good catch. Kernel trace shows a mode-shift: fast path kernels for sequence length 256 dropped ~30% in soft-gate because more requests were clipped to 128 target tokens. That increased per-token overhead.

jay: so we reduced memory but paid cost in kernel efficiency -> net p95 regressed. Any heuristics to avoid that pivot?

maria: proposed tweak: instead of strictly lowering target token count, bias batching to keep sequence-length buckets that preserve cutlass kernels. Algorithm (pseudo):
```
if kv_mem > soft_wm:
  bucket = choose_bucket(preferred_buckets, preserve_kernel=True)
  target_tokens = max(64, base_tokens * scale_for(bucket))
else:
  target_tokens = base_tokens
```

sam: preserve_kernel=True means we'll allow slightly higher memory if it keeps kernel hit-rate high? fine tradeoff if p95 improves. Any numbers?

perf-bot: microexperiment A/B (100k requests each):
- A (naive soft-trim): p95=94ms, KV-frag=31%, cost/tok -2.8%
- B (kernel-aware trim): p95=87ms, KV-frag=24%, cost/tok -1.6%
(so B recovers most perf, slightly worse memory improvement)

kei: B looks promising. We must also avoid oscillation — if we keep allowing mem to surge to preserve kernel, other callers may starve. Did you add hysteresis?

maria: yes: hysteresis window 60s and a gradient-based scaling so we don't flip gates every second. Also a backoff counter per node for repeated hard gates.

ops-bot: Incident note: last week we had a regional spike where hard gating caused user-facing timeouts for streaming clients. Ticket #INC-2026 opened.

maria: Right — to avoid that we plan canary rollout: 5% traffic with kernel-aware soft-gate + 0.5% hard-gate threshold reduction. Monitor p95, rejection-rate, and KV-frag.

jay: what observability surfaces do we need in Console to monitor this?

maria: add per-node metrics: kv_mem_fraction, kv_fragmentation, kernel-hit-rate (by bucket), batch_admit_rate, avg_target_tokens. Also expose a percentile of target_tokens per minute.

sam: one more thought — maybe we can use compacting eviction instead of pure LRU when fragmentation > 40% to reclaim contiguous credit. That reduces eviction churn. Worth prototyping?

kei: agree, but compacting has CPU cost and pauses. Need to profile pause impact. Do a small experiment on low-traffic nodes first.

maria: plan: 1) start 5% canary with kernel-aware soft-gate + hysteresis; 2) collect metrics for 48h; 3) run compacting eviction on a separate pool with low load for 24h; 4) iterate.

sam: thumbs-up. Add a rollback guard: auto-disable if p95 > baseline+15% or rejection_rate > 1% sustained 5m.

jay: also add an eval harness to ensure generation quality doesn't drop when we clip target tokens (some prompts rely on longer continuation).

maria: will add prompt set and automatic quality regression alert.

kei: tagging SRE on the canary window and schedule a quick oncall page if thresholds breach.

maria: thanks all — I'll post the canary config and a short runbook once it's staged. :thumbsup:
